Instantaneously Retarget a Fitted TMLE Without Refitting ML Nuisance Models

Source: R/fit_and_retarget.R
retarget.Rd

Re-runs only the positivity truncation, fluctuation submodel, and Efficient Influence Function (EIF) inference using the cached out-of-fold nuisance predictions stored inside a tmle_fit object. Because nuisance Super Learning accounts for 95–99% of runtime while the targeting fluctuation takes milliseconds, retarget() lets you run positivity sensitivity sweeps, switch estimands, or inspect subgroup effects interactively with zero ML refitting.

Usage

retarget(
  object,
  g_bounds = NULL,
  estimand = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL,
  fluctuation = NULL,
  conf.level = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "tmle_fit" object.

g_bounds

Optional updated positivity bounds ("adaptive", scalar, or c(low, high)). Defaults to the bound currently used in object.

estimand

Optional updated estimand(s) (e.g., c("rr", "or"), "att", "atc", "ate"). Defaults to the estimand in object.

subgroup

Optional unquoted filtering expression (e.g. age >= 65) evaluated on the cached cohort data to perform instant subgroup TMLE re-targeting. When NULL (default), preserves the currently active subgroup; pass subgroup = TRUE to reset back to the full cohort.

fluctuation

Optional updated fluctuation submodel ("logistic", "logistic_covariate", "linear", "none").

conf.level

Confidence level for intervals; defaults to the level stored in object (0.95 initially).

Value

An updated "tmle_fit" object.

Examples

df <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 150, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 1)
fit <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2)) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 3L) |>
  fit(df)
fit_strict <- retarget(fit, g_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95))
fit_ratios <- retarget(fit, estimand = c("ate", "rr", "or"))
fit_older <- retarget(fit, subgroup = age >= 50)
